biography.plain_text: John Palmer was a British gold dealer and timeshare businessman known as “Goldfinger”. He built a substantial property business in Tenerife and was convicted of timeshare fraud in 2001. Earlier, he had been acquitted of knowingly handling gold from the Brink’s-Mat robbery. He was murdered at his Essex home in 2015.

confidence.reason: Detailed obituary, legal case analysis and later police-appeal reporting distinguish the fraud conviction from the separate gold-handling acquittal.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before his notoriety, John Palmer sold paraffin from a lorry and built a scrap-metal business. He then moved into second-hand gold and jewellery dealing in Bristol through Scadlynn, the company he established with business partners. That trade preceded his expansion into holiday-property sales in Spain.

Palmer's Tenerife operation persuaded customers to upgrade their timeshares by promising to resell their existing properties. The supposed resale business was little more than an office and fax machine upstairs. Customers were left paying for two properties when the promised sales failed to materialise. Palmer dismissed his lawyers and defended himself at the trial that ended with an eight-year prison sentence.

confidence.reason: Full institutional-hosted case analysis and detailed obituary support early trades, business formation, the specific deception and self-representation. Convicted conduct is distinguished from unproven allegations.
